title: Shifted Hom from integral constructible complexes preserves the localization unit telescope
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed extension, and let $X$ have Noetherian underlying topological space. Use the actual integral coefficient category and scalar extension $L$ of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and let $K,B$ be integral bounded constructible objects. Let $U$ be restriction of scalars, and let $t_B$ be the scalar localization unit cocone of [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope]: its stages are $B$, its transitions are $\ell\operatorname{id}_B$, its vertex is $ULB$, and its $n$th leg is the adjunction unit followed by $U$ of inverse multiplication by $\ell^n$. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map induced by these legs is an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$\varinjlim_{n\in\mathbf N}\operatorname{Hom}(K,B[q])\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Hom}(K,(ULB)[q]).$$
Equivalently, this cocone has the shifted Hom-colimit property of [def-weil-pbc-hom-colimit-property]. The same assertion holds after reindexing by $\operatorname{ULift}\mathbf N$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: the displayed commutation of Hom with the scalar telescope for bounded constructible K and B

proof.text: Write $R$ for the actual integral coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and $Q$ for passage from complexes of $R$-modules to their ordinary derived category. First fix any complex $C$ zero below an integer $a$. Its scalar sequence has a colimit cocone $c$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-complex-telescope]. All its stages are $C$, so they share the cohomological lower bound $a$. Good truncation at $a$ changes no stage up to the natural truncation isomorphism, since every term below $a$ is zero; transporting $c$ along this isomorphism gives precisely the indicated good-truncated telescope colimit. We will prove shifted Hom continuity for this cocone before using a representative of $B$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3, common lower bound; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2

proof.text: Whisker the complex diagram and its cocone by the equivalence $\operatorname{AsSmall}(\mathbf N)\simeq\mathbf N$. A compatible family out of either diagram is exactly a compatible family out of the other, so the colimit universal property is unchanged; the lower bound is still $a$. For every constructible $R$-module sheaf $M$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-sheaf-hom] applies to this cocone and gives $H(QD,Qc)(M[0])$ in the notation of [def-weil-pbc-hom-colimit-property], for every integer target shift. The field, finite-extension, topologically Noetherian and ordinary-coefficient hypotheses are exactly those of the item.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and its application in Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: For this fixed diagram and cocone, put $P(T)=H(QD,Qc)(T)$. It contains zero, since both Hom groups are zero. An isomorphism $T\simeq T'$ gives isomorphisms of the source Hom diagrams and target groups by precomposition, commuting with all cocone legs, hence transfers $P$. Also $\operatorname{Hom}(T[m],QD_i[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,QD_i\lbrack q-m\rbrack)$, naturally in $i$ and in the cocone legs. Thus $P(T)$ implies $P(T[m])$ for every integer $m$; applying this with $-m$ gives the converse.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and its application in Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: The definition of integral bounded constructibility in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] gives bounded cohomology of $K$ and constructibility of every $H^r(K)$. Take the finite cone witness $F_0,\ldots,F_N=K$ of [lem-sfb-bounded-cohomology-cone-witness] and induct on its index. A term isomorphic to a shifted $H^r(K)[0]$ satisfies $P$ by steps 2–3. Otherwise its witness triangle is $F_i\to F_j\to F_r[n]\to F_i[1]$ with $i,j<r$. Rotation, as in [def-weil-triangulated-category], gives $F_j\to F_r[n]\to F_i[1]\to F_j[1]$. The induction hypothesis and step 3 give $P(F_j)$ and $P(F_i[1])$; [lem-weil-pbc-hom-colimit-extension] gives $P(F_r[n])$, and shifting by $-n$ gives $P(F_r)$. This proves $P(K)$, including when all its cohomology is zero. Thus for every strictly bounded-below $C$ considered in step 1, all its shifted Hom cocones from $K$ are colimits of abelian groups.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and its application in Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: Boundedness of $B$ implies boundedness below, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-localization-complex-model] supplies a strict complex model of its canonical unit cocone $t_B$, with representative isomorphism $e:B\simeq QC$ and vertex isomorphism $v:Q(c_\infty)\simeq ULB$ compatible with every leg. For each $q$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-localization-colimit-transport] to the functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(K,T[q])$ with values in abelian groups. Its premise concerns every strictly bounded-below complex telescope; steps 1–4 prove exactly that premise, including the good-truncated colimit. The conclusion is that this functor sends the lifted canonical cocone $t_B$ to a colimit cocone. No colimit in the derived category itself has been assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and its application in Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: The model's leg equation is $Q(c_n)\,;v=e^{-1}\,;t_{B,n}$. Hence the identification of the stage Hom group by $e$ and of its vertex by $v$ carries $h:K\to B[q]$ at stage $n$ to $h\,;t_{B,n}[q]$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope], $t_{B,n}$ is the adjunction unit followed by restricted inverse multiplication by $\ell^n$. Thus the comparison proved invertible in step 5 is the canonical map in the statement, with transition multiplication by $\ell$. Finally $\operatorname{ULift}\mathbf N\simeq\mathbf N$ via $n\mapsto n.\mathrm{down}$ identifies stages, transitions and legs. Compatible families correspond under this bijection, so their Hom colimits and canonical comparison maps correspond. This proves both indexing versions for every $q$.

tool_uses.why: Fixes the actual ordinary coefficient category and bounded constructibility; essential to avoiding a change to completed or discrete coefficients.

Identifies the resulting comparison with precisely the specified inverse-scalar unit legs.
TR2 supplies the rotation that puts the two known vertices at the endpoints.

Generic closure under distinguished extensions; the rationalization unit has no separate closure lemma.
Provides the actual scalar sequence colimit on complexes, before passage to the derived category.
Supplies all shifted Hom-colimit isomorphisms for a constructible sheaf source with the same coefficient and scheme hypotheses.

Source: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.12 and Prop. 6.8.14(2) proof ('full faithfulness follows from Lemma 6.8.12'), plus HRS Lemma 5.3 for the common lower bound. The coefficient category is the parent's actual integral one. The Lean BoundedConstructible (t.bounded ⊓ IsConstructibleModuleObject of every H^n) matches the hypothesis of lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-sheaf-hom. Checks by step. Steps 1–2: the colimit cocone from the complex telescope, transported along good truncation, matches the hcont cocone of localizationCocone_isColimit_of_model (Lean signature read); the sheaf-hom node then gives H for M[0] in every shift. Step 3: closure under zero, isomorphism and shift is elementary. Step 4: induction on the cone witness; TR2 rotation puts F_j and F_i[1] at the ends, which is the orientation hom-colimit-extension needs over ℕ, a small filtered category; the K=0 case is covered. Step 5: B is bounded below, so the complex model applies and transport gives the ULift version. Step 6: the comparison is the canonical map, and both indexings hold. Not a duplicate: sequential-hom states only factorization; internal-hom-continuity, bounded-below-compactness, scalar-localization-derived-hom and det-lem-constructible-ext-continuity-devissage are other settings or statements.
